questions.question: Rural development mainly focuses on improving the quality of life for:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**rural population**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rural development primarily aims to improve the **quality of life and economic well-being of people living in rural areas**.
 
• The focus areas include **agriculture, education, healthcare, infrastructure, and employment opportunities** for rural communities.
 
• It targets marginalized groups such as small farmers, landless laborers, tribal populations, and women.
 
• Government schemes like **MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act)** and PMAY-G (Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Gramin) are examples of rural development initiatives.
 
• Rural development is crucial for reducing **poverty, rural-urban migration, and regional disparities** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act):**

 
 
• MGNREGA provides a legal guarantee of 100 days of wage employment in a financial year to rural households.
 
• It focuses on creating durable assets like roads, canals, and water conservation structures in rural areas.
 
• This scheme aims to reduce rural poverty and promote livelihood security.
 
 
 
• **PMAY-G (Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Gramin):**
 
 
• It aims to provide affordable housing to rural poor families with basic amenities.
 
• Financial assistance is given to beneficiaries to construct pucca houses.
 
• The scheme promotes women's ownership of houses and social inclusiveness.
 
 
 
• **National Rural Health Mission (NRHM):**
 
 
• NRHM focuses on improving healthcare facilities and reducing maternal and infant mortality in rural areas.
 
• It addresses health disparities by strengthening primary healthcare systems.
 
• Programs like ASHA workers (Accredited Social Health Activists) are key components of NRHM.
 
 
 
• **Key Challenges in Rural Development:**
 
 
• Lack of infrastructure like roads, electricity, and water supply.
 
• Low literacy rates and inadequate healthcare services.
 
• Dependence on agriculture and vulnerability to climate change.
 
• Social issues such as caste discrimination and gender inequality.

questions.question: What is a piece of code which is capable of copying itself and having a detrimental effect, such as corrupting an individual system or destroying its data?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Virus.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A computer virus is a type o**f computer program that, **when executed,** replicates itself by modifying** other computer programs and inserting its own code into** those programs.**
 
• If this replication succeeds, the affected areas are then **said to be "infected" with a computer virus,** a metaphor derived from biological viruses.
 
• Computer **viruses generally require a host program.**
 
• The virus writes its own code into the** host program.**
 
• When the program runs, the written **virus program is executed first,** causing infection and damage.
 
• Worm, **ILOVEYOU, SQL Slammer, Stuxnet, **CryptoLocker, Tinba, Welchia, and Shlayer are some examples of computer viruses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
 

 **Trojan Horse**
 
 
 
• In computing, a Trojan horse is any **malware that misleads** users of its true intent. The term is derived from the** Ancient Greek story **of the deceptive Trojan Horse that led to the fall of the city of Troy.
 
 
 
 

 **Worm**
 
 
 
• A computer worm is a **standalone malware computer program** that replicates itself in order to spread to other computers. It often uses a computer network to spread itself, relying on **security failures** on the target computer to access it. It will use this machine as a** host to scan** and infect other computers. 
 
 
 
 

 **Zombies**
 
 
 
• In computing, a zombie is a computer **connected to the Internet** that has been compromised by a hacker via a computer virus, **computer worm**, or trojan horse program and can be used to** perform malicious tasks** under the remote direction of the hacker.

• The **suspension of Fundamental Rights during an emergency** in India is inspired by the **Weimar Constitution of Germany (1919)**.

• **Emergency Provisions of Indian Constitution**__
 
• These provisions are contained in **Part XVIII** of the Constitution from **Article 352 to 360**.
 
• These provisions enable the Central government to meet any abnormal situation effectively. The rationality behind the incorporation of these provisions in the Constitution is to safeguard the sovereignty, unity, integrity, and security of the country, the democratic political system, and the Constitution.
 
• The Constitution of India has **three types of emergencies**
 __
 
• **​****National Emergency**: This **emergency is provided in Article 352** and the President of India can declare a national emergency when the security of India is threatened on the grounds of wars, external aggression, or armed rebellion
 
• Financial Emergency:
 
 
• It is provided in Article 360 and empowers the President to proclaim a financial emergency if he is not satisfied with a situation that has arisen and the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.
 
 
 
• **State Emergency:**
 
 
• It is provided in** Article 356 and is popularly known as Presidents Rule**.
 
• It empowers the President to issue a proclamation if he is satisfied that a situation has arisen in which the government of a state cannot be worked according to the provisions of the constitution.

questions.question: The information stored in the RAM can be checked with the help of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**BIOS.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) is responsible for performing the Power-On Self-Test (POST) and initializing hardware components during the boot process.**
 
• It can check and verify the information stored in the RAM as part of the POST process.
 
• **BIOS ensures that the RAM is functioning correctly and that data can be accessed properly.**
 
• It provides low-level communication between the hardware and the operating system, enabling further system initialization and operation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hard Disk:** A hard disk is a storage device that retains data even when the system is powered off. It is not involved in directly checking the information in RAM.
 
• **CMOS:** CMOS (Complementary Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor) stores configuration settings for the BIOS, but it does not check RAM data.
 
• **Kernel:** The kernel is a core part of the operating system responsible for managing hardware and software resources. It does not perform RAM checks during boot-up.
 
• **RAM:** RAM (Random Access Memory) is a volatile memory used for temporary storage of data. It requires BIOS to verify its integrity during system initialization.

questions.question: Which of the following hormone helps in regulating blood sugar levels of human body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Insulin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Insulin** is a hormone that plays a central role in regulating **blood sugar levels** in the human body by facilitating the uptake of glucose into cells.
 
• It is secreted by the **beta cells** of the **Islets of Langerhans** in the pancreas, a gland located behind the stomach.
 
• Insulin helps in storing excess glucose as **glycogen** in the liver and muscles, thus preventing hyperglycemia (high blood sugar levels).
 
• A deficiency or resistance to insulin leads to **diabetes mellitus**, a condition characterized by increased blood glucose levels.
 
• Insulin is crucial for maintaining glucose homeostasis, and its role is vital in converting glucose into energy required for cellular functions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Functions of Insulin:**

 
 
• Insulin promotes the uptake of **glucose** by cells, especially in the liver, muscle, and fat tissues.
 
• It inhibits the breakdown of stored glycogen (**glycogenolysis**) and the production of glucose from non-carbohydrate sources (**gluconeogenesis**).
 
• It enhances the synthesis of **fatty acids** in adipose tissues and protein synthesis in muscles.
 
 
 
• **Other Hormones Involved in Blood Sugar Regulation:**
 
 
• **Glucagon:** Secreted by the alpha cells of the pancreas, glucagon increases blood sugar levels by promoting glycogen breakdown and gluconeogenesis.
 
• **Adrenaline:** A hormone released by the adrenal glands, it raises blood glucose levels during stress or emergencies by stimulating glycogenolysis.
 
• **Cortisol:** A stress hormone secreted by the adrenal cortex, it increases blood sugar levels by promoting gluconeogenesis.
 
 
 
• **Conditions Associated with Insulin:**
 
 
• **Type 1 Diabetes:** Caused by the destruction of beta cells, leading to insufficient production of insulin.
 
• **Type 2 Diabetes:** Characterized by insulin resistance, where cells fail to respond to insulin effectively.
 
• **Hyperinsulinemia:** Excessive insulin levels, often associated with conditions like insulin resistance and obesity.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Other Hormones Mentioned in the Options:**
 
 
• **Thymus:** The thymus gland is involved in the immune system and does not regulate blood sugar levels. Its function is to produce T-lymphocytes.
 
• **Adrenaline:** This hormone is secreted by the adrenal glands and raises blood sugar levels during stress but does not regulate it continuously like insulin.
 
• **Testosterone:** A male sex hormone, it is responsible for secondary sexual characteristics and has no role in blood sugar regulation.

questions.question: The ______ lies above the mesopause and is a region in which temperatures increase with height.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is thermosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The thermosphere lies above the mesopause and is a region in which temperatures increase with height.
 
• Thermosphere:
 
 
• In the thermosphere, the temperature rises very rapidly with increasing height.
 
• The ionosphere is a part of this layer.
 
• It extends between 80-400 km. This layer helps in radio transmission.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bc946d2bceb2a062dbac62800db09d1917e1c951b6529055f8a86a303bcca49f.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• There are a total of five atmospheric layers. These are -
 
 
• Troposphere.
 
• Stratosphere.
 
• Mesosphere.
 
• Thermosphere.
 
• Ionosphere: the lowest part of the Thermosphere contains the ionosphere.
 
• Exosphere.
 
 
 
• Stratosphere:
 
 
• It lies beyond the troposphere, up to an altitude of 50 km from the earth's surface.
 
• The temperature in this layer remains constant for some distance but then rises to reach a level of 0°C at 50 km altitude.
 
• This rise is due to the presence of ozone.
 
• This layer is almost free from clouds and associated weather phenomena, making conditions most ideal for flying aeroplanes.
 
 
 
• Exosphere:
 
 
• This is the uppermost layer of the atmosphere extending beyond the ionosphere above a height of about 400 km.
 
• The air is extremely rarefied and the temperature gradually increases through the layer.
 
• Light gases like helium and hydrogen float into space from here.
 
 
 
• Troposphere:
 
 
• It is the lowermost layer of the atmosphere.
 
• The layer starts at Earth's surface and extends 8 to 14.5 km high (5 to 9 miles).
 
• The troposphere contains dust particles and water vapour.
 
• This is the most important layer of the atmosphere because all kinds of weather changes take place only in this layer.
 
• The zone dividing troposphere from the stratosphere is known as the tropopause.

questions.question: Which chemical is used for artificial rain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Silver Iodide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Artificial rain**, also known as cloud seeding, is a process by which specific chemicals are introduced into clouds to stimulate precipitation. The most commonly used chemical for this process is **Silver Iodide**.
 
• **Silver Iodide** serves as an effective nucleating agent because its crystalline structure is similar to that of ice. This similarity allows it to promote the formation of ice crystals in clouds, which grow and eventually fall as precipitation. *Hence, Silver Iodide is widely used in artificial rain creation.*
 
• Apart from Silver Iodide, other substances like **dry ice (solid carbon dioxide)** and **liquid propane** are sometimes used for cloud seeding, but Silver Iodide remains the most effective and widely utilized. *Therefore, the correct answer is Silver Iodide.*
 
• The process of cloud seeding is carried out by dispersing Silver Iodide particles from aircraft or ground-based generators into the atmosphere. Once introduced, these particles encourage the condensation of water vapor into ice crystals, which results in rainfall.
 
• The use of Silver Iodide in cloud seeding has been proven effective in regions experiencing droughts or water scarcity. It has been used extensively in countries like **India, the United States, and China** to combat water shortages and agricultural challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Characteristics of Silver Iodide:**

 
 
• **Silver Iodide** is a yellow powder that is insoluble in water and has a crystalline structure similar to ice, making it ideal for cloud seeding.
 
• It is non-toxic and environmentally safe when used in controlled amounts, although excessive usage may lead to environmental concerns.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Artificial Rain:**
 
 
• Artificial rain is used in **agriculture** to ensure adequate water supply during dry seasons or droughts.
 
• It is also employed in **urban areas** to mitigate air pollution by washing away particulate matter from the atmosphere.
 
• **Example:** In **India**, states like **Maharashtra** and **Karnataka** have conducted cloud seeding experiments to combat drought conditions.
 
 
 
• **Global Usage:**
 
 
• Countries like **China** have invested heavily in artificial rain technology to address water shortages and improve agricultural productivity.
 
• The **United States** uses cloud seeding in regions like **California** to enhance snowfall and water reserves.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Limitations of Cloud Seeding:**

 
 
• Cloud seeding is effective only when there are sufficient moisture and cloud formations in the atmosphere.
 
• It is not a guaranteed method for generating rainfall, as weather conditions play a significant role in its success.
 
 
 
• **Key Developments:**
 
 
• **1946:** The first successful cloud seeding experiment was conducted by **Vincent Schaefer** in the **United States**, using dry ice.
 
• **Modern Applications:** Countries like **India** and **UAE** have adopted advanced cloud seeding technologies for artificial rain generation.

questions.question: The procedure of Impeachment of the President of India is __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the** __Quasi-Judicial Procedure.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• The procedure of Impeachment of the President of India is the Quasi-Judicial Procedure.
 
• **The procedure** begins with the introduction of a bill in either house of Parliament.
 
• The only condition for the initiation of the impeachment of the Indian president is the **‘violation of the constitution**.
 
• None of the presidents of India has faced impeachment so far.
 
• A quasi-judicial body is an** organ of Government other than a Court or Legislature, **which affects the rights of private parties either through adjudication or rulemaking”.
 
• It is not mandatory that a Quasi-Judicial Body has to necessarily be an organization resembling a Court of Law.
 
 
• For example, the Election Commission of India is also a Quasi-Judicial Body but does not have its core functions as a Court of Law.
 
 
 
• Some examples of Quasi-Judicial Bodies in India are the Election Commission of India, the National Green Tribunal, and the Central Information Commission (CIC).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• **Process of Impeachment of the President of India**:

 
 
• When a President is to be impeached for violation of the Constitution, the charge shall be preferred by** either House of Parliament.**
 
• For the motion to be valid, it must be signed by at least one-fourth of the total members of the house where it is introduced
 
• In the case of the Lok Sabha, this means that the motion must be signed by at least one-fourth of the total Lok Sabha members.
 
• A 14-day notice is given to the President of India.
 
• Then, Lok Sabha passes the impeachment charges with a two-thirds majority and sends it to Rajya Sabha.
 
• Then, the Rajya Sabha investigates the charges.
 
• While Rajya Sabha is investigating the charges, the President has the right to sit in the proceedings.
 
• Rajya Sabha agrees to the charges and passes it with a two-thirds majority and the President is removed.

questions.question: The length of the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle is 37 cm and the length of one of its other two sides is 12 cm. What is the area of the triangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Recognize the standard Pythagorean triplet: (12, 35, 37).

If the hypotenuse is 37 cm and one side is 12 cm, the other side (base) is 35 cm.

Area = ½ × base × height

Area = ½ × 35 × 12 = 210 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 210 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Hypotenuse of the right-angled triangle (h) = 37 cm

Length of one side (perpendicular) = 12 cm

**Formula Used:**

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

Area of a right-angled triangle = ½ × Base × Perpendicular

 

 

 12 cm
 Base = b
 Hypotenuse = 37 cm

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the unknown base of the triangle be b.

⇒ 37² = 12² + b²

⇒ 1369 = 144 + b²

⇒ b² = 1369 − 144

⇒ b² = 1225

⇒ b = √1225 = 35 cm

⇒ Area of the triangle = ½ × Base × Perpendicular

⇒ Area = ½ × 35 × 12

⇒ Area = 35 × 6 = 210 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 210 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Common Pythagorean Triplets

Standard triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), (7, 24, 25), (8, 15, 17), (9, 40, 41), and (12, 35, 37). Memorizing these basic sets can drastically reduce calculation time during exams.

Properties of a Right-Angled Triangle

The circumcircle of a right-angled triangle has its center at the exact midpoint of the hypotenuse, meaning the circumradius is always half the length of the hypotenuse (R = h ÷ 2).

Area using Heron's Formula

If only the three sides (a, b, c) of any triangle are known, its area can be calculated as Area = √[s(s − a)(s − b)(s − c)], where s is the semi-perimeter: s = (a + b + c) ÷ 2.
</p

Combined Average = Base average + Net deviation = 80 + 6 = 86 marks.

**∴ The correct answer is 86 marks.**

Number of remaining students = 30 − 18 = 12

questions.question: Let m and n be natural numbers. What is the minimum value of (m + n) such that 33m + 22n is divisible by 121 ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We are given the expression 33m + 22n, which can be factored as 11(3m + 2n).

For this to be divisible by 121 (which is 11 × 11), the term (3m + 2n) must be a multiple of 11.

To minimize the sum (m + n), we evaluate the smallest positive multiple, setting 3m + 2n = 11.

Testing natural numbers: if m = 3 and n = 1, then 3(3) + 2(1) = 11, giving m + n = 4.

Alternatively, if m = 1 and n = 4, then 3(1) + 2(4) = 11, giving m + n = 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: 33m + 22n

Divisor: 121

m and n are natural numbers (m, n ≥ 1).

**Formula Used:**

If a number N is divisible by D, then N = k × D for some positive integer k.

**Calculations:**

⇒ 33m + 22n = 121k

⇒ 11(3m + 2n) = 11 × 11k

⇒ 3m + 2n = 11k

To minimize (m + n), we should take the smallest possible positive integer value for k. Let k = 1.

⇒ 3m + 2n = 11

⇒ 2n = 11 − 3m

Since n must be a natural number, 2n is an even positive integer. Therefore, (11 − 3m) must be an even positive integer.

Let's check possible natural number values for m:

⇒ If m = 1: 2n = 11 − 3(1) = 8 ⇒ n = 4. The sum is m + n = 1 + 4 = 5.

⇒ If m = 2: 2n = 11 − 3(2) = 5 (Not possible, since n would not be an integer).

⇒ If m = 3: 2n = 11 − 3(3) = 2 ⇒ n = 1. The sum is m + n = 3 + 1 = 4.

⇒ If m ≥ 4: 11 − 3m will be negative or zero, which cannot yield a natural number for n.

Thus, the possible pairs of (m, n) for k = 1 are (1, 4) and (3, 1).

The sums are 5 and 4 respectively. The minimum value of (m + n) is 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of its digits at odd positions and the sum of its digits at even positions is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

Linear Diophantine Equations

An equation of the form ax + by = c has integer solutions if and only if the greatest common divisor of a and b perfectly divides c.

Natural Numbers

Natural numbers are the set of positive integers starting from 1 (i.e., 1, 2, 3, 4, ...). Zero, fractions, decimals, and negative numbers are not considered natural numbers.
</p

questions.question: A car starts from point A towards point B, travelling at the speed of 20 km/h. 1(1)/(2)hours later, another car starts from point A and travelling at the speed of 30 km/h and reaches 2(1)/(2)hours before the first car. Find the distance between A and B.

Total time difference = 1.5 hours (late start) + 2.5 hours (early arrival) = 4 hours

⇒ 1 unit = 4 hours, so time taken by Car 1 = 3 × 4 = 12 hours

**Calculations:**

Direct Distance Formula

When travelling the same distance at two different speeds S₁ and S₂ with a known total time difference Δt, Distance = (S₁ × S₂ ÷ |S₁ − S₂|) × Δt.

Average Speed

questions.question: Pravin can do a piece of work in 6 hours. Rishi can do it in 28 hours. With the assistance of Shan, they completed the work in 4 hours. In how many hours can Shan alone do it?

Time taken by Shan alone = Total Work ÷ Shan's Efficiency = 84 ÷ 4 = 21 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 21 hours.**

questions.question: When 416, 888, 1537 and 2245 are divided by the greatest number x, the remainder in each case is the same. The remainder is :
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The greatest number x leaving the same remainder is the HCF of the differences between the consecutive numbers.

Differences = (888 − 416), (1537 − 888), (2245 − 1537) = 472, 649, 708.

HCF of 472, 649, and 708 = 59. So, the greatest number x = 59.

Divide any given number (e.g., 416) by 59 to find the remainder: 416 = 59 × 7 + 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 416, 888, 1537, and 2245.

**Method Used:**

If given numbers a, b, c, and d leave the same remainder when divided by the greatest number x, then x is the HCF of their absolute differences: |a − b|, |b − c|, |c − d|.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Difference 1 = 888 − 416 = 472

⇒ Difference 2 = 1537 − 888 = 649

⇒ Difference 3 = 2245 − 1537 = 708

⇒ Now, find the HCF of 472, 649, and 708.

⇒ Prime factorization of 472 = 2³ × 59

⇒ Prime factorization of 649 = 11 × 59

⇒ Prime factorization of 708 = 2² × 3 × 59

⇒ The common factor in all three differences is 59, so HCF = 59.

⇒ Therefore, the greatest divisor x = 59.

⇒ To find the remainder, divide 416 by 59.

⇒ 416 ÷ 59 = 7 with a remainder of 3.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Greatest Number for Same Remainder

When asked to find the greatest number that divides x, y, and z leaving the same remainder in each case, calculate the HCF of |x − y|, |y − z|, and |z − x|.

Greatest Number for Specific Remainders

To find the greatest number that divides x, y, and z leaving remainders a, b, and c respectively, find the HCF of (x − a), (y − b), and (z − c).

LCM and HCF Formula

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their LCM and HCF: A × B = LCM × HCF.

HCF of Fractions

The HCF of given fractions is calculated as: HCF of Numerators ÷ LCM of Denominators.
</p

questions.question: The mean and median of the data x, y and z are 50 and 35 respectively where z - x = 55, so find y - x.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of x, y, z = Mean × 3 = 50 × 3 = 150.

The median is the middle term. Assuming x ≤ y ≤ z, we get y = 35.

Sum of remaining terms x + z = 150 − 35 = 115.

Given z − x = 55, subtracting this from the sum gives 2x = 60 ⇒ x = 30.

Difference y − x = 35 − 30 = 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Mean of x, y, and z = 50

Median of x, y, and z = 35

z − x = 55

 
 
•

 Mean = 50

**Formula Used:**

Mean = Sum of observations ÷ Total number of observations

**Calculations:**

⇒ Mean = (x + y + z) ÷ 3

⇒ 50 = (x + y + z) ÷ 3

⇒ x + y + z = 150

Assume x ≤ y ≤ z to satisfy the positive difference z − x = 55 and match the option values. The median of three arranged terms is the middle term.

⇒ y = 35

Substitute y = 35 and z = x + 55 into the sum equation:

⇒ x + 35 + (x + 55) = 150

⇒ 2x + 90 = 150

⇒ 2x = 60

⇒ x = 30

Now, substitute x = 30 to find z:

⇒ z = 30 + 55 = 85

The numbers in ascending order are 30, 35, 85, which validates our assumption. The required value is y − x:

⇒ y − x = 35 − 30

⇒ y − x = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

The mean is the average of a set of numbers, calculated by dividing the sum of all observations by the total number of observations.

questions.question: frac{{( {1 + cot θ - cosec θ } )( {1 + tan θ + sec θ } )( {{{sec }²}θ } )}}{{( {sec θ - cos θ } )( {cot θ + tan θ } )}} , 0° < θ < 90°, is equal to:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Put θ = 30° in the given expression.

Numerator = (1 + √3 − 2)(1 + 1/√3 + 2/√3) × (2/√3)² = (√3 − 1)(√3 + 1) × (4/3) = 8/3

Denominator = (2/√3 − √3/2)(√3 + 1/√3) = (1 / 2√3) × (4/√3) = 2/3

Expression = (8/3) ÷ (2/3) = 4

Checking the correct value for θ = 30°: 2 cosec 30° = 2 × 2 = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 cosec θ.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: [ (1 + cot θ − cosec θ)(1 + tan θ + sec θ) × sec² θ ] ÷ [ (sec θ − cos θ)(cot θ + tan θ) ]

**Formula Used:**

sin² θ + cos² θ = 1

tan θ = sin θ / cos θ , cot θ = cos θ / sin θ

sec θ = 1 / cos θ , cosec θ = 1 / sin θ

**Calculations:**

⇒ Numerator = (1 + cos θ / sin θ − 1 / sin θ)(1 + sin θ / cos θ + 1 / cos θ) × sec² θ

⇒ Numerator = [ (sin θ + cos θ − 1) / sin θ ] × [ (cos θ + sin θ + 1) / cos θ ] × sec² θ

⇒ Numerator = [ (sin θ + cos θ)² − 1² ] / (sin θ cos θ) × sec² θ

⇒ Numerator = [ sin² θ + cos² θ + 2 sin θ cos θ − 1 ] / (sin θ cos θ) × sec² θ

⇒ As sin² θ + cos² θ = 1

⇒ Numerator = [ 1 + 2 sin θ cos θ − 1 ] / (sin θ cos θ) × sec² θ

⇒ Numerator = (2 sin θ cos θ / sin θ cos θ) × sec² θ = 2 sec² θ

⇒ Denominator = (1 / cos θ − cos θ)(cos θ / sin θ + sin θ / cos θ)

⇒ Denominator = [ (1 − cos² θ) / cos θ ] × [ (cos² θ + sin² θ) / (sin θ cos θ) ]

⇒ Denominator = (sin² θ / cos θ) × (1 / sin θ cos θ)

⇒ Denominator = sin θ / cos² θ

⇒ Expression = (2 sec² θ) ÷ (sin θ / cos² θ)

⇒ Expression = (2 / cos² θ) × (cos² θ / sin θ)

⇒ Expression = 2 / sin θ = 2 cosec θ

**∴ The correct answer is 2 cosec θ.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pythagorean Identities

Fundamental rules: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1 | sec²θ − tan²θ = 1 | cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1

Reciprocal Identities

Inverses: sinθ = 1/cosecθ | cosθ = 1/secθ | tanθ = 1/cotθ

Quotient Identities

questions.question: LCM of two co-primes x and y is
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

By definition, co-prime numbers share no common factors other than 1.

Because they have no common prime factors, their Lowest Common Multiple (LCM) is simply the product of the two numbers.

LCM(x, y) = x × y = xy

**∴ The correct answer is xy.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Two numbers x and y are co-primes.

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM

**Calculation:**

⇒ For any two co-prime numbers, their Highest Common Factor (HCF) is always 1.

⇒ Applying the formula for the two numbers x and y:

⇒ x × y = HCF(x, y) × LCM(x, y)

⇒ x × y = 1 × LCM(x, y)

⇒ LCM(x, y) = xy

**∴ The correct answer is xy.**

**__Additional Information__**

Co-Prime Numbers

Two numbers are considered co-prime (or relatively prime) if their highest common factor (HCF) is 1. The numbers themselves do not have to be prime numbers (for example, 8 and 15 are composite numbers but co-prime to each other).

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two positive integers a and b, the product of their HCF and LCM is equal to the product of the numbers themselves: HCF × LCM = a × b.

Twin Primes

Twin primes are a pair of prime numbers that have a difference of exactly 2 (e.g., 3 and 5, 11 and 13). All twin primes are naturally co-prime.
</p

questions.question:
Simplify the given expression.

2(x² + y²)² − 3xy(x² + y²) − 2x²y²
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let A = x² + y² and B = xy.

The given expression is 2A² − 3AB − 2B².

Factorising by splitting the middle term: 2A² − 4AB + AB − 2B² = (2A + B)(A − 2B).

Substitute A and B back into the factors.

⇒ [2(x² + y²) + xy][(x² + y²) − 2xy] = (2x² + 2y² + xy)(x² + y² − 2xy).

**∴ The correct answer is (2x² + 2y² + xy)(x² + y² − 2xy).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: 2(x² + y²)² − 3xy(x² + y²) − 2x²y²

**Method Used:**

Factorisation using the middle-term splitting method by substituting complex terms.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let us substitute (x² + y²) = a and xy = b.

⇒ The given expression transforms to: 2a² − 3ab − 2b²

⇒ Splitting the middle term (−3ab) as (−4ab + ab):

⇒ 2a² − 4ab + ab − 2b²

⇒ Taking common factors from the groups:

⇒ 2a(a − 2b) + b(a − 2b)

⇒ Taking (a − 2b) common:

⇒ (2a + b)(a − 2b)

⇒ Now, substitute back the original values of a = x² + y² and b = xy:

⇒ [2(x² + y²) + xy] [(x² + y²) − 2xy]

⇒ Expanding the brackets:

⇒ (2x² + 2y² + xy)(x² + y² − 2xy)

**∴ The correct answer is (2x² + 2y² + xy)(x² + y² − 2xy).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Middle Term Splitting Method

For a quadratic expression of the form Ax² + Bx + C, the middle term Bx is split into two terms such that their sum is B and their product is A × C.

Substitution Method in Algebra

Substitution simplifies complex algebraic expressions by replacing larger groups of variables with a single variable, turning them into basic polynomials that are easier to factorise.

Standard Algebraic Identities

Although not required to match the options, the term (x² + y² − 2xy) is equal to (x − y)² as per the standard identity (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab.
